title: Garlicky Jerusalem artichokes and watercress on toast

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a simple staple: artichokes, butter, oil, garlic, hazelnuts, bread, goat's cheese and watercress.

supermarket.reason: Jerusalem artichokes, watercress, soft goat's cheese and hazelnuts are all stocked by mainstream supermarkets in March at everyday prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan and a toaster or grill, and frying, toasting and tossing a salad are all beginner techniques.

works.reason: Allowing about 125g of artichoke, a slice of toast, cheese and a handful of dressed watercress each makes a sound lunch for four, and the frying time suits thinly sliced artichokes.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is a fair allowance for scrubbing and slicing 500g of artichokes plus garlic and hazelnuts, and the 15 minute cook matches the frying step.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, nothing unlisted appears, and wholemeal bread matches the bread id.

seasonal_feel.reason: Late-March watercress and the last of the artichokes make a fitting spring lunch, and 100g of dressed watercress piled on each toast is a real component rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are plain, clear British English that a beginner can follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Wholemeal toast with vegetables, cheese, nuts and greens is a balanced, appealing lunch a family would make again.
